title: From a metric to a dashboard to an alert
caption: Illustrative numbers: a small web service whose error rate rises after a bad deploy.

steps.title: Your app counts what it does
steps.text: The app keeps counters and gauges: requests served, errors, how long each request took. It publishes them as plain text at /metrics, so anything can read them.
steps.idea: A metric is a named number, with labels, sampled over time.

steps.title: Prometheus scrapes it
steps.text: Prometheus pulls the numbers on a schedule and stores each one with its timestamp. Stored over time they form a time series you can look back on.
steps.idea: Prometheus pulls. Your app does not need to know who is watching.

steps.title: Ask questions with PromQL
steps.text: PromQL asks the stored series questions. rate(http_requests_total[5m]) is requests per second over the last five minutes, and dividing the error rate by it gives the share of requests that fail.
steps.idea: rate() turns an ever-growing counter into something you can read: a speed.

steps.title: Grafana draws the answers
steps.text: Grafana stores no metrics itself. A dashboard panel is a query that Grafana runs against Prometheus and draws as a graph, a number or a gauge.
steps.idea: A dashboard is saved questions, asked again every few seconds.

steps.title: Something goes wrong
steps.text: A bad deploy starts failing requests. The error rate climbs from 0.5% to 6.5%, and the panel shows it before any customer writes in.
steps.idea: Watching the error rate is how you notice before your users tell you.

steps.title: A rule fires an alert
steps.text: An alert rule is a PromQL condition that must hold for a while, such as an error rate above 5% for 5 minutes. When it does, Prometheus sends the alert to Alertmanager, which groups it and decides who to tell.
steps.idea: The 'for' duration stops a single blip from waking anyone.

steps.title: A person is told, and looks
steps.text: Alertmanager notifies the on-call engineer by chat, email or pager. They open the dashboard, see which service is failing and when it began, and go and fix it.
steps.idea: Alerts say that something is wrong. Dashboards say where to look.
